title: MARS
subtitle: Model-agnostic Biased Object Removal without Additional Supervision for Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation

problem.head: WSSS with image-level labels also segments class-related backgrounds: biased objects
messages: Two images of the boat and train classes with their ground truth
The WSSS output also covers the sea and the railroad: biased objects
35% of the classes in PASCAL VOC 2012 have such biased objects
problem.note: Paper Fig. 1(c) and 1(d) · examples of biased objects in the boat and train classes on PASCAL VOC 2012

separate.head: Observation 1: inside the WSSS output, USS features separate the biased object from the target
bottom: (a) USS features of the whole image
fails to detect the biased object
(b) WSSS features in the WSSS output
cannot find it: the features are biased
(c) USS features in the WSSS output
separate.card_sub: The USS and WSSS features come from the same ViT-B backbone.
messages: The WSSS output for the boat class includes a biased object next to the boats
(a) Without the WSSS output, USS features split the whole image instead
(b) WSSS features cannot separate the biased object: they are biased themselves
(c) USS features split the WSSS output into the boats (pink) and the biased object (orange)
separate.note: Paper Fig. 2 · integration with WSSS and USS on one PASCAL VOC 2012 image · USS: unsupervised semantic segmentation

select.head: Observation 2: the biased object is closer to the backgrounds of other images
select.left_title: Distance to the backgrounds of other images
left_rows: Background regions of other images (by the USS method)
right_text: The average of the top α% centroids that are most apart from the background centroids of all training images (α = 0.40).
More than 85% of the selected centroids are target centroids on PASCAL VOC 2012 (paper Fig. 8).
messages: K-means gives two candidate objects: which one is the biased object?
The candidate with the short distance to the backgrounds of other images is the biased object
The centroids most apart from the backgrounds give the debiased centroid of each class
select.note: Paper Fig. 3 and Sec. 3.2 · distances between the two separated objects and the background regions of other images in the same dataset

debias.head: From the conventional WSSS label to the debiased label
cards: The label from the trained WSSS method includes the biased objects.
WSSS foreground that is not similar to the debiased centroids becomes the biased class.
During training, the teacher's predictions fill the biased class, which restores non-biased objects.
debias.legend: biased class (−1) in the debiased label
messages: Three examples from the paper: the train, boat and dog classes
Conventional WSSS: the railroad and the sea are labelled as train and boat
Debiased labels: the biased objects are removed, and so are non-biased parts of the dog
Complementing restores the non-biased objects, and the biased objects stay removed
debias.note: Paper Fig. 7 · effect of the proposed components (Secs. 3.1 to 3.4) on PASCAL VOC 2012 images

results.head: Segmentation results on the validation sets: RS+EPM and MARS
cards: IoU of the train · boat classes
messages: RS+EPM: biased objects remain in the segmentation results
Model-agnostic: +6.3 on IRNet, +6.3 on SEAM, +2.2 on AdvCAM and +3.3 on RS+EPM (mIoU, VOC 2012 val)
results.note: Supplementary Fig. G (examples) · paper Tables 3 and 5 and Fig. 9 (numbers) · no additional supervision or dataset
